### mysql-routine-declare-order

DECLARE statements out of MySQL's order: needs a rewrite. MySQL takes DECLARE only at the start of a BEGIN ... END block, with variables and conditions first, then cursors, then handlers; this routine declares out of that order, so its CREATE fails.

Fix: Move each DECLARE to the start of its block, in the order variables and conditions, cursors, handlers.

Documentation: MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual, DECLARE Statement.

### mysql-routine-definer

A DEFINER naming a user other than the target user: needs a rewrite. The routine runs as its DEFINER, a named user other than the user that creates it on Aurora MySQL; when that account does not exist on the target cluster, every call \(or every trigger and event firing\) fails with error 1449.

Fix: Set DEFINER to the target user \(or CURRENT\_USER\), or create the named account on the target before the routine is used.

Documentation: MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual, Stored Object Access Control; Amazon Aurora User Guide, Role-based privilege model.

### mysql-routine-dependency-not-moved

A routine that names a table or routine not moved in the same step: blocks the move. The routine reads, writes or calls an object that is not created on the target in the same step, so it fails when it runs \(or, for a trigger, cannot be created\) until that object moves too.

Fix: Move the named tables and routines in the same step as this routine, or move the routine in the step that moves them.

Documentation: MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual, CREATE PROCEDURE and CREATE FUNCTION Statements; MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual, CREATE TRIGGER Statement.

### mysql-routine-dynamic-sql

Dynamic SQL the checks cannot read: behaves differently. The routine prepares and runs SQL held in a user variable, so the statement checks cannot see what it runs on the target; the string literals the routine assigns to that variable are checked, but it may hold other text at run time.

Fix: Review the SQL the routine builds and run it on the target before cutover, or replace the dynamic SQL with static statements the checks can read.

Documentation: MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual, Prepared Statements.

### mysql-routine-file-output

Writing a file on the database server: needs a rewrite. SELECT ... INTO OUTFILE and INTO DUMPFILE write a file on the database server, which needs the FILE privilege; the Aurora MySQL administrative role \(rds\_superuser\_role\) does not include it.

Fix: Write the file to Amazon S3 with SELECT ... INTO OUTFILE S3, after granting the AWS\_SELECT\_S3\_ACCESS role.

Documentation: Amazon Aurora User Guide, Saving data from an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster into text files in an Amazon S3 bucket.

### mysql-routine-handler

A handler MySQL refuses: needs a rewrite. A handler is one MySQL refuses: an UNDO handler, an SQLSTATE that is not five characters or is in class 00, error code 0, a condition name no enclosing block declares, or the same condition handled twice in one block.

Fix: Use CONTINUE or EXIT, a valid SQLSTATE or error code, declare the condition before the handler, and handle each condition once per block.

Documentation: MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual, DECLARE ... HANDLER Statement; DECLARE ... CONDITION Statement.

### mysql-routine-kill

Ending another session or query with KILL: behaves differently. KILL ends another user's connection or query only with CONNECTION\_ADMIN, which on Aurora MySQL a user has only through rds\_superuser\_role or an explicit grant, so the statement fails when the routine runs as any other user.

Fix: Call mysql.rds\_kill or mysql.rds\_kill\_query instead, or make sure the user the routine runs as holds CONNECTION\_ADMIN.

Documentation: MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual, KILL Statement; Amazon Aurora User Guide, Role-based privilege model; Aurora MySQL stored procedure reference.

### mysql-routine-load-file

Reading a server file with LOAD\_FILE\(\): behaves differently. LOAD\_FILE\(\) reads a file on the database server and needs the FILE privilege, which the Aurora MySQL administrative role \(rds\_superuser\_role\) does not include, so on Aurora it returns NULL instead of the file.

Fix: Load the file from Amazon S3 with LOAD DATA FROM S3 into a table, and read the table instead.

Documentation: MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual, String Functions and Operators \(LOAD\_FILE\); Amazon Aurora User Guide, Loading data into an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster from text files in an Amazon S3 bucket.

### mysql-routine-mode-deprecated

An sql\_mode MySQL 8.0 deprecates: informational. The routine's sql\_mode includes a mode MySQL 8.0 deprecates; it still works on Aurora MySQL today, but a later version line may remove it.

Fix: Keep the mode on Aurora MySQL 8.0; drop it only when the target line removes it, padding CHAR values with RPAD in place of PAD\_CHAR\_TO\_FULL\_LENGTH, and dropping the zero-date and division-by-zero modes only on a line whose strict mode includes their effect.

Documentation: MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual, Server SQL Modes.

### mysql-routine-mode-removed

An sql\_mode MySQL 8.0 removed: needs a rewrite. The routine was created under an sql\_mode MySQL 8.0 removed, and every Aurora MySQL line in standard support is 8.0 or later; setting that mode fails, so the routine cannot be created under its own sql\_mode.

Fix: Drop the removed mode from the routine's sql\_mode \(NO\_AUTO\_CREATE\_USER has no replacement; a removed combination mode becomes the modes it stood for\) and check the routine still behaves the same.

Documentation: MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual, What Is New in MySQL 8.0 \(Features Removed in MySQL 8.0\); Server SQL Modes.

### mysql-routine-mode-unknown

An sql\_mode MySQL 8.0 does not have: needs a rewrite. The routine's sql\_mode names a mode MySQL 8.0 does not have \(for example a MariaDB mode\), so setting it fails and the routine cannot be created under its own sql\_mode.

Fix: Replace the mode with its MySQL equivalent, or drop it, and check the routine still behaves the same.

Documentation: MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual, Server SQL Modes.

### mysql-routine-plugin-install

Installing or removing a plugin or component: needs a rewrite. Installing or removing a plugin or component writes to the mysql system database, which Aurora MySQL users cannot change; Aurora manages its plugins itself.

Fix: Remove the statement; turn on a supported feature through the DB cluster parameter group instead.

Documentation: Amazon Aurora User Guide, Comparing Aurora MySQL version 3 and MySQL 8.0 Community Edition.

### mysql-routine-replication-control

Replication and binary log control statements: needs a rewrite. Replication and binary log control statements need REPLICATION\_SLAVE\_ADMIN, BINLOG\_ADMIN or SUPER, which the Aurora MySQL administrative role \(rds\_superuser\_role\) does not include; Aurora manages replication through its own stored procedures.

Fix: Call the Aurora MySQL procedures instead \(mysql.rds\_set\_external\_source, mysql.rds\_start\_replication, mysql.rds\_stop\_replication\), or move the step out of the routine.

Documentation: Amazon Aurora User Guide, Aurora MySQL stored procedure reference; Role-based privilege model.

### mysql-routine-restricted-session-variable

Setting a restricted session system variable: needs a rewrite. Setting the session value of this system variable is restricted: it needs SESSION\_VARIABLES\_ADMIN, SYSTEM\_VARIABLES\_ADMIN or SUPER, which the Aurora MySQL administrative role \(rds\_superuser\_role\) does not include, so the statement fails when the routine runs.

Fix: Remove the SET, or set the value in the DB cluster or DB parameter group when every session needs it.

Documentation: MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual, System Variable Privileges; Amazon Aurora User Guide, Role-based privilege model.

### mysql-routine-server-shutdown

Stopping or restarting the server: needs a rewrite. SHUTDOWN and RESTART need the SHUTDOWN privilege, which the Aurora MySQL administrative role does not include; Aurora instances are stopped and rebooted through the RDS API.

Fix: Remove the statement; reboot or stop the instance with the RDS console, CLI or API.

Documentation: MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual, SHUTDOWN Statement; RESTART Statement; Amazon Aurora User Guide, Role-based privilege model.

### mysql-routine-set-global

Setting a global or persisted system variable: needs a rewrite. Setting a global or persisted system variable needs SUPER or SYSTEM\_VARIABLES\_ADMIN, which the Aurora MySQL administrative role \(rds\_superuser\_role\) does not include, so the statement fails when the routine runs.

Fix: Set the variable in the DB cluster or DB parameter group instead, or set its session value if the routine only needs it for itself.

Documentation: Amazon Aurora User Guide, Role-based privilege model; Working with parameter groups.

### mysql-routine-sql-log-bin

Turning binary logging off for the session: needs a rewrite. Turning binary logging off for a session \(sql\_log\_bin\) needs SUPER, SYSTEM\_VARIABLES\_ADMIN or SESSION\_VARIABLES\_ADMIN, which the Aurora MySQL administrative role does not include, so the statement fails when the routine runs.

Fix: Remove the SET sql\_log\_bin statement; to keep changes out of replication, filter them on the replica or run them outside the replicated schema.

Documentation: MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual, Server System Variables \(sql\_log\_bin\); Amazon Aurora User Guide, Role-based privilege model.

### mysql-routine-unparseable

A routine whose CREATE statement does not read as MySQL: needs a rewrite. The routine's CREATE text could not be read: its header, its quoting or its compound statements \(BEGIN ... END, IF, CASE, LOOP, WHILE, REPEAT and their labels\) do not close as MySQL requires, so it cannot be checked or carried as is.

Fix: Re-collect the routine with SHOW CREATE, or fix the text so it loads on the source MySQL, then run the check again.

Documentation: MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual, CREATE PROCEDURE and CREATE FUNCTION Statements; Compound Statement Syntax.

### mysql-routine-v80-found-rows

SQL\_CALC\_FOUND\_ROWS and FOUND\_ROWS\(\), deprecated in MySQL 8.0: informational. MySQL 8.0.17 deprecates the SQL\_CALC\_FOUND\_ROWS modifier and FOUND\_ROWS\(\); they still run on Aurora MySQL 3, but a later version line may remove them.

Fix: Keep the routine as it is for now; when you next change it, count the rows with a separate SELECT COUNT\(\*\) on the same conditions, without LIMIT.

Documentation: MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual, Information Functions \(FOUND\_ROWS\).

### mysql-routine-v80-group-by-direction

GROUP BY with ASC or DESC, removed in MySQL 8.0: needs a rewrite. MySQL 8.0.13 removed the ASC and DESC qualifiers of GROUP BY columns, so on Aurora MySQL 3 and later the statement no longer parses and the routine cannot be created.

Fix: Drop ASC or DESC from the GROUP BY and add ORDER BY with the same columns and directions.

Documentation: MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual, What Is New in MySQL 8.0 \(Features Removed in MySQL 8.0\).

### mysql-routine-v80-group-by-sort

A SELECT that relied on GROUP BY sorting its rows: behaves differently. MySQL 5.7 returned GROUP BY results sorted by the grouped columns; MySQL 8.0 no longer sorts them, so on Aurora MySQL 3 and later this SELECT \(or the cursor reading it\) can return its rows in another order, and a grouped subquery or INSERT ... SELECT with LIMIT can keep other rows.

Fix: Add ORDER BY with the grouped columns to the SELECT wherever the routine depends on the order of its rows \(a cursor loop, a LIMIT at any level, a result returned to the caller\).

Documentation: MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual, What Is New in MySQL 8.0 \(Features Removed in MySQL 8.0\); ORDER BY Optimization.

### mysql-routine-v80-query-cache-hint

The SQL\_CACHE modifier and the query cache statements, removed in MySQL 8.0: needs a rewrite. MySQL 8.0 removed the query cache with its SQL\_CACHE modifier and its FLUSH QUERY CACHE and RESET QUERY CACHE statements, so on Aurora MySQL 3 and later the statement no longer parses and the routine cannot be created.

Fix: Drop SQL\_CACHE from the SELECT and drop the FLUSH or RESET QUERY CACHE statement; cache the result in the application or in Amazon ElastiCache if the routine relied on it.

Documentation: MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual, What Is New in MySQL 8.0 \(Features Removed in MySQL 8.0\).

### mysql-routine-v80-removed-function

A function MySQL 8.0 removed: needs a rewrite. The routine calls a function MySQL 8.0 removed, so on Aurora MySQL 3 and later the call fails when the routine runs.

Fix: Replace PASSWORD\(\) with the server's own account management, ENCRYPT\(\), ENCODE\(\), DECODE\(\) and DES\_ENCRYPT\(\)/DES\_DECRYPT\(\) with AES\_ENCRYPT\(\)/AES\_DECRYPT\(\) or SHA2\(\); re-encrypt stored values the old functions wrote.

Documentation: MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual, What Is New in MySQL 8.0 \(Features Removed in MySQL 8.0\).

### mysql-routine-v80-removed-spatial-function

A spatial function name MySQL 8.0 removed: needs a rewrite. The routine calls a spatial function by a name MySQL 8.0 removed \(the 5.7 names without the ST\_ or MBR prefix\), so on Aurora MySQL 3 and later the call fails when the routine runs.

Fix: Call the ST\_ name of the same function \(ST\_AsText\(\), ST\_X\(\), ST\_Length\(\) for GLength\(\), MBREquals\(\) for MBREqual\(\)\) or its MBR name for the bounding-box tests \(MBRContains\(\), MBRWithin\(\)\), and check the results: 8.0 spatial functions honour the geometry's spatial reference system.

Documentation: MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual, What Is New in MySQL 8.0 \(Features Removed in MySQL 8.0\); Spatial Function Reference.

### mysql-routine-v80-removed-system-variable

A system variable MySQL 8.0 removed: needs a rewrite. The routine sets or reads a system variable MySQL 8.0 removed, so on Aurora MySQL 3 and later the statement fails with an unknown system variable when the routine runs.

Fix: Use the 8.0 name \(transaction\_isolation for tx\_isolation, transaction\_read\_only for tx\_read\_only, log\_error\_verbosity for log\_warnings\), or drop the statement for a variable with no replacement \(the query cache, old\_passwords, secure\_auth, the InnoDB file format variables\).

Documentation: MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual, What Is New in MySQL 8.0 \(Features Removed in MySQL 8.0\); MySQL Shell, Upgrade Checker Utility.

### mysql-routine-v80-reserved-word

A word MySQL 8.0 reserves, used as an identifier: needs a rewrite. The routine uses as a name \(a parameter, variable, label, column or table\) a word that MySQL 8.0 reserves, so on Aurora MySQL 3 and later the statement no longer parses and the routine cannot be created.

Fix: Quote the name with backticks wherever the routine writes it \(`rank`\), or rename it, and do the same in the statements that call the routine or read the column.

Documentation: MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual, Keywords and Reserved Words; Preparing Your Installation for Upgrade.

### mysql-routine-v84-removed-function

A function MySQL 8.4 removed: needs a rewrite. The routine calls WAIT\_UNTIL\_SQL\_THREAD\_AFTER\_GTIDS\(\), which MySQL 8.4 removed, so on Aurora MySQL version 8.4 the call fails when the routine runs.

Fix: Call WAIT\_FOR\_EXECUTED\_GTID\_SET\(\) instead, with the same GTID set and timeout.

Documentation: MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual, What Is New in MySQL 8.4 since MySQL 8.0 \(Features Removed\).

### mysql-routine-v84-removed-statement

A statement MySQL 8.4 removed: needs a rewrite. MySQL 8.4 removed FLUSH HOSTS and the MASTER and SLAVE forms of the replication statements, so on Aurora MySQL version 8.4 the statement no longer parses and the routine cannot be created.

Fix: Use TRUNCATE TABLE performance\_schema.host\_cache for FLUSH HOSTS, and the 8.4 forms of the others: SHOW BINARY LOG STATUS, SHOW BINARY LOGS, SHOW REPLICA STATUS, SHOW REPLICAS, RESET BINARY LOGS AND GTIDS, RESET REPLICA, PURGE BINARY LOGS, START REPLICA, STOP REPLICA and CHANGE REPLICATION SOURCE TO.

Documentation: MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual, What Is New in MySQL 8.4 since MySQL 8.0 \(Features Removed\).

### mysql-routine-v84-removed-system-variable

A system variable MySQL 8.4 removed: needs a rewrite. The routine sets or reads a system variable MySQL 8.4 removed, so on Aurora MySQL version 8.4 the statement fails with an unknown system variable when the routine runs.

Fix: Use the 8.4 name \(binlog\_expire\_logs\_seconds for expire\_logs\_days, authentication\_policy for default\_authentication\_plugin, replica\_ and source\_ names for the slave\_ and master\_ ones\), or drop the statement for a variable with no replacement.

Documentation: MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual, What Is New in MySQL 8.4 since MySQL 8.0 \(Features Removed\); MySQL Shell, Upgrade Checker Utility.

### mysql-routine-v84-reserved-word

A word MySQL 8.4 reserves, used as an identifier: needs a rewrite. The routine uses as a name \(a parameter, variable, label, column or table\) a word that MySQL 8.4 reserves, so on Aurora MySQL version 8.4 the statement no longer parses and the routine cannot be created.

Fix: Quote the name with backticks wherever the routine writes it \(`qualify`\), or rename it, and do the same in the statements that call the routine or read the column.

Documentation: MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual, Keywords and Reserved Words; MySQL Shell, Upgrade Checker Utility.

### postgresql-routine-dependency-not-moved

A routine that names a table or routine not moved in the same step: blocks the move. The routine reads, writes or calls an object that is not created on the target in the same step, so it fails when it runs \(or, for a trigger, cannot be created\) until that object moves too.

Fix: Move the named tables and routines in the same step as this routine, or move the routine in the step that moves them.

Documentation: PostgreSQL documentation, CREATE FUNCTION; PostgreSQL documentation, CREATE TRIGGER.

### postgresql-routine-extension-not-offered

A routine that uses an extension the target Aurora PostgreSQL version does not offer: blocks the move. The routine depends on an extension that Aurora PostgreSQL does not offer on the target version line, so it cannot be created there.

Fix: Replace what the extension provides with SQL or an extension the target version offers, move to a version line that offers it, or keep that logic outside the database.

Documentation: Extension versions for Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL.

### postgresql-routine-language

A function or procedure in a language Aurora PostgreSQL does not run: blocks the move. Aurora PostgreSQL runs PL/pgSQL, SQL and the trusted languages it offers as extensions, but no untrusted language \(plpythonu, plpython3u, plperlu, pltclu\) and no C or internal function a customer loads, so this routine cannot be created on the target.

Fix: Rewrite the routine in PL/pgSQL or SQL, or in a trusted language Aurora PostgreSQL offers on the target version \(PL/Perl, PL/Tcl, PL/v8, PL/CoffeeScript or PL/LiveScript\).

Documentation: Amazon Aurora User Guide, Working with Trusted Language Extensions for PostgreSQL; Extension versions for Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL.

### postgresql-routine-superuser-security-definer

A SECURITY DEFINER routine owned by a superuser: needs a rewrite. A SECURITY DEFINER routine runs with its owner's privileges, and no Aurora PostgreSQL role is a superuser \(rds\_superuser is not one\), so on the target it runs with fewer privileges than on the source and can fail where it relied on superuser rights.

Fix: Give the routine an owner role on the target with only the privileges it needs, check that nothing in it needs superuser rights, and set an explicit search\_path on it.

Documentation: Amazon Aurora User Guide, Understanding PostgreSQL roles and permissions; PostgreSQL documentation, CREATE FUNCTION.

### postgresql-routine-unparseable

A routine whose CREATE statement does not parse: needs a rewrite. PostgreSQL's own parser cannot read this routine's CREATE statement, or its PL/pgSQL or SQL body, as one statement of the routine's kind, so it cannot be loaded as collected.

Fix: Re-collect the routine with pg\_get\_functiondef or pg\_get\_triggerdef, or correct the statement so it parses, then check it again.

Documentation: PostgreSQL documentation, CREATE FUNCTION; CREATE PROCEDURE; CREATE TRIGGER.

## Routine rewrites: what changes on its own

Generated from `src/catalog/routine_rewrites/*.toml` (#1937; field definitions: `src/shared/catalog/routine_rewrites.py`). Each rewrite changes a routine's header only, never its body; each is recorded with its rule, its reason and a diff that never holds a literal, and a routine that still fails a check after its rewrites still needs attention. <!-- claim: tests/unit/tools/routines/test_routine_rewrites.py::test_the_record_never_holds_a_literal, tests/unit/tools/routines/test_routine_rewrites.py::test_a_definer_rewrite_never_changes_the_body, tests/unit/tools/routines/test_routine_rewrites.py::test_a_search_path_pin_never_changes_the_body, tests/unit/tools/routines/test_routine_rewrites.py::test_other_failed_checks_keep_the_routine_needing_attention, tests/unit/tools/routines/test_routine_rewrites.py::test_the_same_input_gives_byte_identical_output --> A rewrite may still change how the routine runs, as each row says: a DEFINER or owner rewrite makes a routine that runs as its definer run with the target user's privileges, which its record notes, and a search_path pin keeps the source's name resolution even for a caller whose path differs. <!-- claim: tests/unit/tools/routines/test_routine_rewrites.py::test_a_definer_rewrite_notes_when_the_routine_runs_as_the_target_user, tests/unit/tools/routines/test_routine_rewrites.py::test_an_owner_rewrite_notes_a_security_definer_routine, tests/unit/tools/routines/test_routine_rewrites.py::test_a_security_definer_routine_pins_the_search_path -->

| Rule | Sources | Targets | Kinds | Rewrites | Resolves |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`mysql-routine-definer-to-target-user`](#mysql-routine-definer-to-target-user) | mysql | Aurora MySQL | procedure, function, trigger, event | a DEFINER clause naming a user other than the target user is replaced by one naming the target user, and a text with no clause whose metadata names another user gets one; a CURRENT_USER form is left as it is, and a target user with no host is user@% <!-- claim: tests/unit/tools/routines/test_routine_rewrites.py::test_a_named_definer_becomes_the_target_user, tests/unit/tools/routines/test_routine_rewrites.py::test_a_definer_that_is_the_target_user_or_current_user_is_left_as_is, tests/unit/tools/routines/test_routine_rewrites.py::test_a_text_with_no_definer_clause_gets_one_only_when_its_metadata_names_another_user, tests/unit/tools/routines/test_routine_rewrites.py::test_a_target_user_with_no_host_is_any_host --> | [`mysql-routine-definer`](#mysql-routine-definer) |
| [`postgresql-routine-owner-to-target-user`](#postgresql-routine-owner-to-target-user) | postgresql | Aurora PostgreSQL | function, procedure | a function or procedure is owned by the target user; its CREATE statement names no owner, so only the record changes <!-- claim: tests/unit/tools/routines/test_routine_rewrites.py::test_the_owner_becomes_the_target_user --> | - |
| [`postgresql-routine-pin-search-path`](#postgresql-routine-pin-search-path) | postgresql | Aurora PostgreSQL | function, procedure | a SECURITY DEFINER function or procedure that sets no search_path gets a SET search_path clause naming the source's effective path, to keep its name resolution (no pg_temp is added); a SECURITY INVOKER routine, or one whose body reads, sets or resets the search_path, is left as it is <!-- claim: tests/unit/tools/routines/test_routine_rewrites.py::test_a_security_definer_routine_pins_the_search_path, tests/unit/tools/routines/test_routine_rewrites.py::test_an_existing_set_search_path_is_left_as_is, tests/unit/tools/routines/test_routine_rewrites.py::test_a_security_invoker_routine_is_not_pinned, tests/unit/tools/routines/test_routine_rewrites.py::test_a_body_that_reads_or_changes_the_search_path_is_not_pinned --> | - |
| [`routine-dependency-order`](#routine-dependency-order) | mysql, postgresql | Aurora MySQL, Aurora PostgreSQL | function, procedure, trigger, event | every routine is created after the routines of the step it names, ties in routine id order; a dependency cycle is reported, and its routines are created together in routine id order <!-- claim: tests/unit/tools/routines/test_routine_dependencies.py::test_routines_follow_what_they_call_ties_in_id_order, tests/unit/tools/routines/test_routine_dependencies.py::test_cycles_are_reported_and_never_followed_round --> | - |

### mysql-routine-definer-to-target-user

The DEFINER clause names the target user. A DEFINER naming an account that does not exist on the target makes every call fail with error 1449, so the DEFINER clause is rewritten to the user that creates the routine on Aurora MySQL; only that clause of the header changes, never the body; a routine that runs as its definer \(SQL SECURITY DEFINER, and every trigger and event\) then runs with the target user's privileges, and its record says so.

Documentation: MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual, Stored Object Access Control; Amazon Aurora User Guide, Role-based privilege model.

### postgresql-routine-owner-to-target-user

A function or procedure is owned by the target user. A function's CREATE statement names no owner, so on Aurora PostgreSQL the routine is owned by the user that creates it; the record names that user in place of the source owner, and the statement does not change; a SECURITY DEFINER routine then runs with the target user's privileges, and its record says so.

Documentation: PostgreSQL documentation, CREATE FUNCTION; PostgreSQL documentation, ALTER FUNCTION.

### postgresql-routine-pin-search-path

A SECURITY DEFINER routine pins the source's effective search\_path. A SECURITY DEFINER routine that sets no search\_path resolves unqualified names in its caller's search\_path, so a SET search\_path clause naming the source's effective path is added to its header to keep the name resolution it had on the source \(it is not hardening: no pg\_temp is added, and a caller whose path differs now resolves names in the pinned one\); a routine that already sets one, or whose body reads, sets or resets the search\_path, is left as it is.

Documentation: PostgreSQL documentation, CREATE FUNCTION.

### routine-dependency-order

Routines and triggers are created in dependency order. Each routine and trigger is created after the routines it names, ties in routine id order, so what it calls exists when it is created; a dependency cycle is reported, and its routines are created one after another in routine id order.

Documentation: PostgreSQL documentation, CREATE TRIGGER; MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual, CREATE TRIGGER Statement.

## Write intents: serving a carried write the target's way

Generated from `src/catalog/write_intents/*.toml` and `src/catalog/carried_writes.toml` (#1362; field definitions: `src/shared/catalog/write_intents.py`). A write group moves as one unit (ADR-031 Decision 1 Amendment 9), so it can carry a member whose own score on the group's engine is low. Below the floor, the member's intent is read from its parsed facts (`src/agents/referee/carried_writes.py`) and the designer input and the risk register name the engine's approach below; routing never reads it.

- `carried_write_fit_floor` = 50: A write-group member whose own score on the group's engine is below this is carried there by its table's other writes, not by its own fit: the designer is told the statement's intent and the target-native way to serve it, and the risk register raises it \(#1362\). On the bundled samples every carried member below 50 scores 26 or less, so 30 would list the same 14 statements \(#1359\).

| Intent | What it is for |
|---|---|
| [`bulk-status-flip`](#bulk-status-flip) | Sets one column (a status, a flag) to one value on every row a predicate picks, no full key value addressing them. |
| [`consistency-repair`](#consistency-repair) | Re-aligns a value kept in step with another table wherever the two disagree. |
| [`duplicate-cleanup`](#duplicate-cleanup) | Removes rows that repeat another row's natural key, keeping one. |
| [`multi-reference-delete`](#multi-reference-delete) | Removes every row that refers to one entity through any of several columns, for example when the entity is deleted. |
| [`orphan-cleanup`](#orphan-cleanup) | Removes rows, or clears references, whose parent row no longer exists. |
| [`retention-delete`](#retention-delete) | Removes rows once they pass an age or expiry cut-off, run on a schedule. |
| [`set-based-write`](#set-based-write) | Any other maintenance write: model what it is for, the target's way, not its SQL. |

### bulk-status-flip

Bulk status flip: Sets one column \(a status, a flag\) to one value on every row a predicate picks, no full key value addressing them.

| Engine | Approach | Documentation |
|---|---|---|
| DynamoDB | Make the change at the event that causes it, with an UpdateItem on that item; for a time-based flip, store the deadline and read the status from it, or index the pending items in a sparse GSI and have a scheduled job update each with a conditional UpdateItem. | Amazon DynamoDB Developer Guide, Take advantage of sparse indexes; section on condition expressions |
| DocumentDB | Run an updateMany over an index on the predicate fields (a partial index of the pending documents), in batches, or make the change where the event happens. | Amazon DocumentDB Developer Guide, Managing Amazon DocumentDB indexes |
| OpenSearch | Index the status from the source's change events, or run an update by query in batches. | OpenSearch documentation, Update by query API |
| ElastiCache | Update the key at the event that changes it; a cached status expires with its source. | Valkey documentation, EXPIRE command reference |
| Aurora PostgreSQL | Keep the UPDATE, in batches over an index on the predicate (a partial index of the pending rows). | PostgreSQL documentation, Partial Indexes |
| Aurora MySQL | Keep the UPDATE, in batches (UPDATE ... LIMIT) over an index on the predicate columns. | MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual, UPDATE Statement |

### consistency-repair

Consistency repair sweep: Re-aligns a value kept in step with another table wherever the two disagree.

| Engine | Approach | Documentation |
|---|---|---|
| DynamoDB | Enforce the rule at write time: the write that changes the source value also updates each copy, in the same UpdateItem when both are on one item or in a TransactWriteItems over the items (up to 100); collocate one-to-one entities in one item collection so the join disappears. For a wider fan-out, a DynamoDB Streams consumer on the source item updates the copies with a conditional UpdateItem; a sweep kept as a safety net is a scheduled batch job over a sparse GSI, one conditional UpdateItem per item. | Amazon DynamoDB Developer Guide, Managing complex workflows with DynamoDB transactions; Change data capture for DynamoDB Streams |
| DocumentDB | Embed the value so there is one copy, or update the copies where the source changes, in a multi-document transaction or from a change stream consumer; a sweep kept as a safety net runs in batches over an index on the copied field. | Amazon DocumentDB Developer Guide, Transactions; Using change streams with Amazon DocumentDB |
| OpenSearch | Re-index the documents that carry the copy from the source's change events, or look the value up at query time; never sweep the index. | Amazon OpenSearch Service Developer Guide, Overview of Amazon OpenSearch Ingestion |
| ElastiCache | Rewrite or invalidate the cached copy where the source value changes (write-through), instead of sweeping. | Amazon ElastiCache User Guide, section on caching strategies |
| Aurora PostgreSQL | Keep the rule in one place: a constraint where it can express the rule, a trigger on the source table that updates the copy, or the rule enforced in the write path that changes the source value; a view can derive the value instead of storing a copy. The sweep stays only as a scheduled safety net. | PostgreSQL documentation, Triggers; Constraints |
| Aurora MySQL | Keep the rule in one place: a constraint where it can express the rule, a trigger on the source table that updates the copy, or the rule enforced in the write path that changes the source value; a view can derive the value instead of storing a copy. The sweep stays only as a scheduled safety net. | MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual, Using Triggers; CHECK Constraints |

### duplicate-cleanup

Duplicate clean-up: Removes rows that repeat another row's natural key, keeping one.

| Engine | Approach | Documentation |
|---|---|---|
| DynamoDB | Make the natural key the item's primary key (or write a uniqueness item for it in the same TransactWriteItems) and put with a ConditionExpression of attribute_not_exists, so a duplicate is never stored and nothing needs cleaning up. | Amazon DynamoDB Developer Guide, section on condition expressions |
| DocumentDB | Remove the existing duplicates once, then create a unique index on the natural key fields and upsert on that key, so a duplicate insert fails instead of being cleaned up later. | Amazon DocumentDB Developer Guide, Managing Amazon DocumentDB indexes |
| OpenSearch | Use the natural key as the document _id, so indexing the same entity again overwrites one document. | OpenSearch documentation, Index document API |
| ElastiCache | Key the entry by its natural key and write it with SET NX, so writing it twice keeps one. | Valkey documentation, SET command reference |
| Aurora PostgreSQL | Remove the existing duplicates once, then add a unique constraint on the natural key and write with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so duplicates cannot be written. | PostgreSQL documentation, INSERT (ON CONFLICT clause) |
| Aurora MySQL | Remove the existing duplicates once, then add a unique index on the natural key and write with INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE, so duplicates cannot be written. | MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual, INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE Statement |

### multi-reference-delete

Delete by any of several references: Removes every row that refers to one entity through any of several columns, for example when the entity is deleted.

| Engine | Approach | Documentation |
|---|---|---|
| DynamoDB | Give each reference a GSI (or keep the rows in the entity's item collection), Query each one for the entity and delete what it returns with BatchWriteItem; run it where the entity is deleted, or from a DynamoDB Streams consumer on that delete, never as a Scan. | Amazon DynamoDB Developer Guide, Using Global Secondary Indexes in DynamoDB; Change data capture for DynamoDB Streams |
| DocumentDB | Index each reference field and run one deleteMany per field (or one $or over the indexed fields) where the entity is deleted, or from a change stream consumer. | Amazon DocumentDB Developer Guide, Managing Amazon DocumentDB indexes; Using change streams with Amazon DocumentDB |
| OpenSearch | Map the reference fields as keyword and delete by query on them from the pipeline that handles the entity's delete. | OpenSearch documentation, Delete by query API |
| ElastiCache | Keep a set of the entity's dependent keys and remove them with the entity (UNLINK). | Valkey documentation, UNLINK command reference |
| Aurora PostgreSQL | Index each reference column, so the OR reads the indexes (a bitmap OR) instead of the table, or declare the foreign keys with ON DELETE CASCADE. | PostgreSQL documentation, Combining Multiple Indexes |
| Aurora MySQL | Index each reference column, so the OR reads the indexes (an index merge union) instead of the table, or declare the foreign keys with ON DELETE CASCADE. | MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual, Index Merge Optimization |

### orphan-cleanup

Orphan clean-up: Removes rows, or clears references, whose parent row no longer exists.

| Engine | Approach | Documentation |
|---|---|---|
| DynamoDB | Enforce the rule where the parent is deleted: delete or update its dependents in the same TransactWriteItems (up to 100 items), or, for a wider fan-out, from a DynamoDB Streams consumer on the parent's REMOVE events; keep the dependents in the parent's item collection (the same partition key) so one Query finds them. A sweep that must stay is a scheduled batch job over a sparse GSI of the reference attribute. | Amazon DynamoDB Developer Guide, Managing complex workflows with DynamoDB transactions; Change data capture for DynamoDB Streams |
| DocumentDB | Embed dependents the parent owns in the parent document, so they go with it; otherwise remove or update them where the parent is deleted, in a multi-document transaction or from a change stream consumer. | Amazon DocumentDB Developer Guide, Transactions; Using change streams with Amazon DocumentDB |
| OpenSearch | Delete the dependents with the parent from the pipeline that indexes them (a delete by query on the parent id), or denormalize the parent's fields into each dependent so nothing is left dangling. | OpenSearch documentation, Delete by query API |
| ElastiCache | Delete the dependent keys with the parent (in one MULTI/EXEC, or keep them in one hash under the parent's key), or give them the parent's expiry. | Valkey documentation, Transactions |
| Aurora PostgreSQL | Declare the foreign key with ON DELETE CASCADE or ON DELETE SET NULL, so the database keeps the rule at write time; keep the sweep only for rows written before the constraint. | PostgreSQL documentation, Constraints chapter, Foreign Keys section |
| Aurora MySQL | Declare the InnoDB foreign key with ON DELETE CASCADE or ON DELETE SET NULL, so the database keeps the rule at write time; keep the sweep only for rows written before the constraint. | MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual, FOREIGN KEY Constraints |

### retention-delete

Retention delete: Removes rows once they pass an age or expiry cut-off, run on a schedule.

| Engine | Approach | Documentation |
|---|---|---|
| DynamoDB | Use Time to Live: write an epoch-seconds expiry attribute (the item's date plus the retention period) only on the items the cut-off applies to, the statement's other conditions included, remove it when those conditions stop holding, and enable TTL on it, so DynamoDB deletes expired items in the background with no write cost; TTL deletes within days, not at the second, so a read that must not see an expired item filters on the attribute, and a DynamoDB Streams consumer can archive what TTL removes. | Amazon DynamoDB Developer Guide, Using time to live (TTL) in DynamoDB |
| DocumentDB | Create a TTL index on a date field set only on the documents the cut-off applies to, the statement's other conditions included (a document without the field never expires), and remove the field when those conditions stop holding; DocumentDB deletes expired documents in the background, not at the exact time, and the deletes consume I/O like any write, so a read that must not see an expired document filters on the field. | Amazon DocumentDB Developer Guide, section on time to live (TTL) indexes |
| OpenSearch | Write to time-based indexes behind a rollover alias and let an Index State Management policy delete each index once it passes the retention period, instead of deleting documents one by one. | Amazon OpenSearch Service Developer Guide, Index State Management in Amazon OpenSearch Service |
| ElastiCache | Set the expiry when the key is written (SET with EX, or EXPIRE), so the cache drops it at the cut-off with no sweep. | Valkey documentation, EXPIRE command reference |
| Aurora PostgreSQL | Keep the scheduled DELETE, in small batches over an index on the date column, or range-partition the table on that column and drop whole old partitions (the pg_partman extension can schedule it). | Amazon Aurora User Guide, Managing PostgreSQL partitions with the pg_partman extension |
| Aurora MySQL | Keep the scheduled DELETE, in small batches (DELETE ... LIMIT) over an index on the date column, or range-partition the table on that column and drop old partitions with ALTER TABLE ... DROP PARTITION. | MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual, Partitioning |

### set-based-write

Set-based maintenance write: Any other maintenance write: model what it is for, the target's way, not its SQL.

| Engine | Approach | Documentation |
|---|---|---|
| DynamoDB | Model what the statement is for, not its SQL: enforce the rule where the data is written (UpdateItem or TransactWriteItems), react to the change with a DynamoDB Streams consumer, or run a scheduled batch job over a sparse GSI of the rows it picks; never a Scan of the table. | Amazon DynamoDB Developer Guide, Best practices for designing and architecting with DynamoDB |
| DocumentDB | Model what the statement is for: make the change where the data is written, from a change stream consumer, or in batches over an index that selects the rows; never a collection scan. | Amazon DocumentDB Developer Guide, Using change streams with Amazon DocumentDB |
| OpenSearch | Re-index the affected documents from the source's change events, or run an update or delete by query in batches. | OpenSearch documentation, Update by query API |
| ElastiCache | Make the change where the source is written, or let the keys expire; a cache holds no set to sweep. | Amazon ElastiCache User Guide, section on caching strategies |
| Aurora PostgreSQL | Keep the statement, in batches over an index on its predicate. | PostgreSQL documentation, Indexes chapter |
| Aurora MySQL | Keep the statement, in batches over an index on its predicate. | MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual, Optimization and Indexes |
